  <h2 id="project-ai-title">Allowed AI Use</h2>
  <p>In challenges and the project, AI is allowed as support for reasoning, debugging, revision, planning or checking. In the exam, only the tools explicitly authorized on Brio are allowed. In all cases, the final deliverable must remain verifiable, personal and consistent with the instructions. You must understand, test and be able to explain any submitted code, text, source, result or interpretation. When AI influences an important part of an evaluated deliverable, keep a short trace: tool used, purpose of help, affected part and verification done. The official requirements posted on Brio always prevail.</p>

  <h2 id="project-check-title">Before each milestone</h2>
  <p>Each project submission should be readable by someone who opens the repository without hearing you explain it.</p>
  <ol class="clean-steps">
  <li>Check the date, submission location and expected file on Brio.</li>
  <li>Render the relevant Quarto documents and open the produced HTML files.</li>
  <li>Check that the GitHub repository contains useful files and no temporary files.</li>
  <li>Reread the question, data, results and limitations as an external reader.</li>
  <li>Make sure team contributions are visible and coherent.</li>
  </ol>
  </div>

  <p>The project is more open than the challenges. It assesses your ability to make reasoned choices and make them readable.</p>

  <article class="resource-hub-card"><h3>Communication</h3><p>Make the work understandable for someone discovering the project.</p></article>

  <h2 id="project-data-title">Data and responsibility</h2>
  <p>The project asks for real autonomy, but that autonomy comes with responsibility for provenance, rights and data protection.</p>
  </div>
  <div class="reading-map">
  <article><h3>Provenance</h3><p>The source must be identifiable, cited and stable enough to be found again.</p></article>
  <article><h3>Usage rights</h3><p>The license or terms should allow use in the course context.</p></article>
  <article><h3>Sensitive data</h3><p>Unnecessary personal or identifying information should not be shared in a public repository.</p></article>
  <article><h3>Limitations</h3><p>Biases, missing values, filters and important transformations must be explained.</p></article>
  </div>
